# STAT 110 (synthetic) — Midterm 1 outline

Current as of this week. This outline replaces earlier versions.

## In scope

- T1 Conditional probability — see Notes §1
- T2 Two-way tables: row and column percentages — see Notes §2
- T3 Bayes' rule — covered in lecture; notes to be posted
- T4 Grouped summaries — see Notes §3

## Not on this midterm

- Hypothesis testing (moved to Midterm 2 this year)

## Reporting rule for every answer

Report every proportion as a percentage rounded to **one decimal place**, and
name the reference group in words. Write "40.0% of commuters", not "0.4",
"40%", or "2/5". Answers without the reference group lose one point.

| Topic | What your work shows | What remains |
|---|---|---|
| Conditional probability | Correct Q3, Q4, and the question that reversed the reference group | An unaided recheck later, before the exam |
| Two-way tables | Not assessed yet | Review row versus column percentages and try independently |
| Bayes’ rule | Not taught or assessed here | Obtain the missing lecture notes, then review and practise |
| Grouped summaries | Not assessed yet | Review summaries per group, output rows, and valid comparisons |

“Not assessed” means **I don’t know whether you understand it**, rather than that you’ve failed it. Q2 also supplies no performance evidence because you requested its answer without attempting it.

**Hypothesis testing is excluded this year**, despite appearing on last year’s paper. Your recent answers correctly follow the percentage and reference-group reporting rule.

The next useful step is **two-way tables**, followed by grouped summaries, while obtaining the Bayes’ rule notes. I saved this assessment and next steps in your [learning record](study/stat-110/midterm-1/learning-record.md).
